extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, licensees, patent agents, and practitioners interacting with Indian patent administration (Controller/High Court)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards under Indian patent law covering compulsory licences, government use, related-patent licences, patent agents, offences, Controller powers, and inventor-mention procedures. Focused on how applications, oppositions, terms, and disputes should be handled before the Controller and High Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller directs service and publication on prima facie case for compulsory licence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Controller is satisfied, upon consideration of an application for compulsory licence, that a prima facie case has been made out, he shall direct the applicant to serve copies of the application upon the patentee and any other person appearing from the register to be interested in the patent in respect of which the application is made, and shall publish the application in the official journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule references: Sections 86-90; Form-17. This is the initial procedural step that triggers the opposition period and subsequent hearing procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition timeframe and contents for compulsory licence applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee or any other person desiring to oppose the application may, within two months from the date of publication of the application or within such further time as the Controller may allow, give to the Controller notice of opposition. The notice of opposition shall include grounds on which the application is opposed and the terms and conditions of the licence, if any, the opponent is prepared to grant to the applicant and shall be accompanied by evidence in support of the opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponent must also serve a copy of the notice and evidence on the applicant and notify the Controller when service has been effected. Form-14 referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on further statements or evidence without Controller leave
rubrics_metrics.description: No further statement or evidence shall be delivered by either party except with the leave of or on requisition by the Controller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits late additions to the record unless expressly permitted by the Controller; intended to keep proceedings timely and orderly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing scheduling and notice period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller shall forthwith fix a date and time for the hearing of the case and shall give the parties not less than ten days' notice of such hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure specified in sub-rules (2) to (5) of rule 62 shall, so far as may be, apply to the procedure for hearing under this rule as they apply to the hearing in opposition proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller refusal where prima facie case not made out; applicant's right to request hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If, upon consideration of the evidence, the Controller is satisfied that a prima facie case has not been made out, he shall notify the applicant accordingly, and unless the applicant requests to be heard in the matter the Controller shall refuse the application. The applicant shall make such a request within one month from the date of such notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant requests hearing within the time allowed, Controller shall give opportunity to be heard and determine whether application may proceed and issue a speaking order expeditiously. Reference: Rule 62.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective when settling royalty and remuneration for licences
rubrics_metrics.description: That the royalty and other remuneration, if any, reserved to the patentee or other person beneficially entitled to the patent, is reasonable, having regard to the nature of the invention, the expenditure incurred by the patentee in making the invention or in developing it and obtaining a patent and keeping it in force and other relevant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 90 lists multiple objectives (a–i) for licence terms; royalty reasonableness must consider invention nature and patentee expenditure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that the invention be worked to fullest extent with reasonable profit to licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patented invention is worked to the fullest extent by the person to whom the licence is granted and with reasonable profit to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller aims to ensure licence enables effective commercial working, not just token use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability at reasonably affordable prices
rubrics_metrics.description: That the patented articles are made available to the public at reasonably affordable prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-interest pricing objective when setting licence terms under Section 90.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for non-exclusive licences
rubrics_metrics.description: That the licence granted is a non-exclusive licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 90(a–i) includes non-exclusivity as a default objective unless otherwise justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-assignability of licensee's right
rubrics_metrics.description: That the right of the licensee is non-assignable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller generally prefers licences that are personal to the licensee and non-transferable, except where assignment accompanies assignment of patent (see related provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence term preference — balance term of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: That the licence is for the balance term of the patent unless a shorter term is consistent with public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller determines appropriate term; default is remainder of patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predominant purpose of supply in Indian market (export permissibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the licence is granted with a predominant purpose of supply in the Indian market and that the licensee may also export the patented product, if need be in accordance with the provisions of sub-clause (iii) of clause (a) of sub-section (7) of section 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes domestic supply while allowing export subject to statutory provisions (e.g., Section 92A considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for semiconductor technology — public noncommercial use
rubrics_metrics.description: That in the case of semi-conductor technology, the licence granted is to work the invention for public noncommercial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 90(h) identifies sector-specific public-use limitation for semiconductor technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export permission when licence remedies anti-competitive practice
rubrics_metrics.description: That in case the licence is granted to remedy a practice determined after judicial or administrative process to be anti-competitive, the licensee shall be permitted to export the patented product, if need be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 90(i) permits export when compulsory licence remedies anti-competitive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of licence terms on licensee application after 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms and conditions of a licence settled by the Controller may be revised upon application by the licensee after a period of not less than twelve months, on the ground that the terms and conditions settled have proved to be more onerous than originally expected and that in consequence the licensee is unable to work the invention except at a loss; however, no such application shall be entertained a second time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows one-time reconsideration of onerous terms after operational experience; safeguard against repeated challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence by licensee where patentee's conditions prejudice working of non-patented materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Controller is satisfied on an application for compulsory license that the manufacture, use or sale of materials not protected by the patent is prejudiced by reason of conditions imposed by the patentee upon the grant of licences under the patent, or upon the purchase, hire or use of the patented article or process, he may, subject to the provisions of Section 84, order the grant of licences under the patent to such customers of the applicant as he thinks fit as well as to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 88(a) addresses tying/restrictive licensing practices that prejudice trade in unpatented materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller power to cancel or amend existing licence when granting compulsory licence to licensee-applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application for compulsory license is made by a person being the holder of a licence under the patent, the Controller may, if he makes an order for the grant of a licence to the applicant, order the existing licence to be cancelled, or may, if he thinks fit, instead of making an order for the grant of a licence to the applicant, order the existing licence to be amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 88(b) gives Controller remedial flexibility vis-à-vis pre-existing licences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence across multiple patents held by same patentee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more patents are held by the same patentee and an applicant for a compulsory licence establishes that the reasonable requirements of the public have not been satisfied with respect to some only of the said patents, then, if the Controller is satisfied that the applicant cannot efficiently or satisfactorily work the licence granted to him under those patents without infringing the other patents held by the patentee and if those patents involve important technical advancement or considerable economic significance in relation to the other patents, he may, by order, direct the grant of a licence in respect of the other patents also to enable the licensee to work the patent or patents in regard to which a licence is granted under section 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 88 addresses patent thickets/poison-pill situations where working one patent requires freedom under related patents; Controller may extend compulsory licences to enable effective working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for licence for related patents (Section 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after the grant of a patent, any person who has the right to work any other patented invention, either as patentee or as licensee thereof, may apply to the Controller for the grant of a licence of the first mentioned patent on the ground that he is prevented or hindered without such licence from working the other invention efficiently or to the best advantage possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory ground enabling cross-licensing orders to remove blocking patents that impair working of another invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's satisfaction criteria for related-patent licence
rubrics_metrics.description: No order under such an application shall be made unless the Controller is satisfied – (i) that the applicant is able and willing to grant, or procure the grant to the patentee and his licensees if they so desire, of a licence in respect of the other invention on reasonable terms; and (ii) that the other invention has made a substantial contribution to the establishment or development of commercial or industrial activities in the territory of India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 91(b)(i–ii) requires reciprocity (applicant must be willing to license back on reasonable terms) and that the other invention contributed substantially to Indian commercial/industrial activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller may grant licence on such terms and non-assignability for related patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If Controller satisfied that the grounds alleged have been established by the applicant, he may make an order on such terms as he thinks fit granting a licence under the first mentioned patent and a similar order under the other patent if so requested by the proprietor of the first mentioned patent. However, such a licence granted by the Controller shall be non-assignable except with the assignment of the respective patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure as mentioned in Sections 87–90 shall apply to licences granted under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government declaration enabling compulsory licences (Section 92)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Central Government is satisfied, in respect of any patent in force in circumstances of national emergency or in circumstances of extreme urgency or in case of public non-commercial use, that it is necessary that compulsory licenses should be granted ... it may make a declaration to that effect by notification in the Official Gazette, and thereupon the Controller shall, on application made at any time after the notification by any person interested, grant to the applicant a licence under the patent on such terms and conditions as he thinks fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 92 creates a mechanism for government-initiated declarations (e.g., national emergency, public health) that alter the landscape for compulsory licences; procedure references to Sections 83, 87–90 apply with some exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms objective for government-initiated licences — lowest prices consistent with reasonable advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: In settling the terms and conditions of a licence granted under this section, the Controller shall endeavour to secure that the articles manufactured under the patent shall be available to the public at the lowest prices consistent with the patentees deriving a reasonable advantage from their patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 92(ii) emphasizes public health/price objectives when licences are granted following a government notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure exceptions in national emergency or extreme urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Controller is satisfied that it is necessary in (i) a circumstance of national emergency; or (ii) a circumstance of extreme urgency; or (iii) a case of public non-commercial use ... the procedure as mentioned in Section 87 shall not apply. However, the Controller shall, as soon as may be practicable, inform the patentee of the patent relating to the application for such non-application of Section 87.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 92(iv) allows accelerated/modified procedure in emergencies (examples include public health crises such as AIDS, TB, Malaria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence for manufacture and export of pharmaceutical products (Section 92A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licence shall be available for manufacture and export of patented pharmaceutical product to any country having insufficient or no manufacturing capacity in the pharmaceutical sector for the concerned product to address public health problems, provided compulsory licence has been granted by such country or such country has allowed importation of the patented pharmaceutical products from India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller shall grant such compulsory licence solely for manufacture and export under specified terms; provisions without prejudice to other export mechanisms under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'pharmaceutical products' for Section 92A
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pharmaceutical products' means any patented product, or product manufactured through a patented process, of the pharmaceutical sector needed to address public health problems and shall be inclusive of ingredients necessary for their manufacture and diagnostic kits required for their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad inclusive definition covers active ingredients and diagnostic kits relevant to public health export licences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of compulsory licence (Section 94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee or any other person deriving title or interest in the patent, may make an application for termination of compulsory licence granted under Section 84 on the ground that the circumstances that gave rise to the grant thereof no longer exist and such circumstances are unlikely to recur. The holder of the compulsory licence shall have the right to object to such termination. While considering such an application, the Controller shall take into account that the interest of the person, who had previously been granted the licence, is not unduly prejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller balances patentee's changed circumstances with protection of licensee's legitimate interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'use for purposes of Government' (Section 99)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is said to be used for the purpose of Government if it is made, used, exercised or vended for the purposes of Central Government, a State Government or a Government undertaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 99 sets the scope of 'government use' across central, state and government undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use when invention recorded/tested by government before priority date — royalty-free
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention has, before the priority date of the relevant claim of the complete specification, been duly recorded in a document, or tested or tried, by or on behalf of the government or a government undertaking, otherwise than in consequence of the communication of the invention directly or indirectly by the patentee ..., any use of the invention by the Central Government or any person authorized in writing by it for the purposes of government may be made free of any royalty or other remuneration to the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 100(a) creates a royalty-free exception where government had independently recorded/tested the invention prior to priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use where invention not previously recorded/tested — remuneration and High Court reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention has not been so recorded or tried, any use of the invention made by the Central Government ... shall be made upon terms as may be agreed upon between the Central Government or any person authorised by Central Government and the patentee, or, as may in default of agreement be determined by the High Court on a reference under Section 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 100(b–c) provides negotiation-first approach with High Court fallback for determining terms/remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate remuneration standard for government use
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of any such use of any patent, the patentee shall be paid not more than adequate remuneration in the circumstances of each case, taking into account the economic value of the use of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 100 sets adequacy-of-remuneration standard tied to economic value rather than full fair-market royalty in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and timing of authorisation by Central Government
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorisation by the Central Government in respect of an invention may be given either before or after the patent is granted and either before or after the acts in respect of which such authorisation is given or done, and may be given to any person, whether or not he is authorised directly or indirectly by the applicant or the patentee to make, use, exercise or vend the invention or import the machine, apparatus or other article or medicine or drug covered by such patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 100(e) permits flexible timing and delegation for government authorisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and information duties when government uses invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention has been used by or with the authority of the Central Government for the purposes of government then except in case of national emergency or other circumstances of extreme urgency or for non-commercial use, the government shall notify the patentee as soon as practicable of the fact and furnish him with such information as to the extent of the use of the invention as he may, from time to time, reasonably require. Where the invention has been used for the purposes of a government undertaking, the Central Government may call for such information as may be necessary for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and reporting obligations apply except in emergency or non-commercial use situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to sell non-commercially and purchaser rights following government use
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to make, use, exercise and vend an invention for the purposes of government shall include the right to sell on non-commercial basis, the goods which have been made in exercise of that right, and a purchaser of goods so sold, and a person claiming through him, shall have the power to deal with the goods as if the Central Government or the person authorised by the Central Government were the patentee of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 100 grants downstream purchasers quasi-patentee powers to deal with government-sold goods non-commercially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of government use on contractual licence/assignment provisions (Section 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of any licence, assignment or agreement granted or made between the patentee ... and any person other than the Central Government shall be of no effect so far as those provisions— (i) restrict or regulate the use for the purposes of government of the invention, or of any model, document or information relating thereto, or (ii) provide for the making of payments in respect of any use of the invention ... for the purposes of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private contractual clauses cannot fetter government use or require payments that would impede government use; reproductions/publications connected with government use are not copyright infringements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of payments between patentee and assignor/exclusive licensee when government use occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where by virtue of sub-section (3) of section 100, payments are required to be made ... and where in respect of such patent there is an exclusive licensee authorised under his licence to use the invention for the purposes of government, such sum shall be shared by the patentee and such licensee in such proportions, if any, as may be agreed upon between them or as may in default of agreement be determined by the High Court on a reference under section 103 to be just, having regard to any expenditure incurred by the licensee in developing the said invention or in making payments to the patentees other than royalties or other benefits determined by reference to the use of the invention in consideration of the licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation of compensation considers development expenditure and prior payments; High Court resolves disputes in default of agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government acquisition of inventions (Section 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Central Government may, if satisfied that it is necessary that an invention which is the subject of an application for a patent or a patent should be acquired from the applicant or the patentee for a public purpose, publish a notification to that effect in the Official Gazette, and thereupon the invention or patent and all rights in respect of the invention or patent shall ... stand transferred to and be vested in the Central Government. Notice of the acquisition shall be given to the applicant, and, where a patent has been granted, to the patentee and other persons appearing in the register as having an interest in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition is a statutory transfer to the State for public purpose, followed by notice to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation considerations on acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Central Government shall pay to the applicant, or as the case may be, the patentee and other persons appearing on the register as having an interest in the patent such other compensation as may be agreed upon ... or, as may, in default of agreement, be determined by the High Court on a reference under section 103 to be just having regard to the expenditure incurred in connection with the invention and, in the case of a patent, the term thereof, the period during which and the manner in which it has already been worked (including the profits made during such period by the patentee or by his licensee whether exclusive or otherwise) and other relevant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High Court considers multiple factors including expenditure, patent term, working history, profits and other relevant factors when determining just compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference of disputes to High Court and High Court procedural powers (Section 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute as to the exercise by the Central Government or a person authorised by it of the powers conferred by section 100, or as to terms for the use of an invention for the purposes of government thereunder or as to the right of any person to receive any part of a payment ... or as to the amount of compensation payable for the acquisition of an invention ... may be referred to the High Court by either party to the dispute. In such proceedings the Central Government may petition by way of counter-claim for revocation of the patent on any ground upon which a patent may be revoked under section 64; and whether a patentee is or is not a party to the proceedings, put in issue the validity of the patent without petitioning for its revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 103 grants the High Court broad jurisdiction and allows the Government to attack patent validity in disputes about use/compensation; confidentiality procedures and references to referees/commissioners/arbitrators are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential disclosure to advocate or independent expert in public interest disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: If in such proceedings any question arises whether an invention has been recorded, tested or tried ... and the disclosure of any document regarding the invention, or of any evidence of the test or trial thereof, would, in the opinion of the Central Government, be prejudicial to the public interest, the disclosure may be made confidentially to the advocate of the other party or to an independent expert mutually agreed upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects sensitive government information while permitting adversarial testing via counsel or mutually agreed independent expert.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Court regard to prior benefits/compensation received
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining under this section any dispute between the Central Government and any person as to terms for the use of an invention for the purposes of government, the High Court shall have regard to any benefit or compensation which that person or any person from whom he derives title, may have received, or may be entitled to receive, directly or indirectly in respect of the use of the invention in question for the purposes of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior or anticipated benefits/payments are relevant in adjudicating fair compensation or terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to official referee, commissioner or arbitrator by High Court
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceedings under this section, the High Court may at any time order the whole proceedings or any question or issue of fact arising therein to be referred to an official referee, commissioner or an arbitrator on such terms as the High Court may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High Court may delegate factual or technical questions to experts/arbitrators for determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special disposal where inventor was government servant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention claimed in a patent was made by a person who at time it was made was in the service of the Central Government or of a State Government or was an employee of a government undertaking and the subject-matter of the invention is certified by the relevant government ... to be connected with the work done in the course of the normal duties of the government servant or employee ... then any dispute of the nature referred to in sub-section (1) relating to the invention shall be disposed of by the Central Government conformably to the provisions of this section so far as may be applicable, but before doing so the Central Government shall give an opportunity to the patentee and such other parties as it considers have an interest in the matter to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special internal government disposition applies to inventions by government employees, but affected parties must be given an opportunity to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file and prosecute patent applications; register of patent agents (Section 126–127)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application can be filed and prosecuted by the Applicant himself or through a registered Indian patent agent. The Register of Patent Agents containing the names and addresses of all the registered patent agents is available at www.ipindia.nic.in. The Patents Act read with the Patents Rules prescribe the qualifications and the eligibility for becoming a patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may self-file or use registered agents; Controller General publishes examination notification and register information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for registration as a patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to apply for registration as a patent agent, one has to be a citizen of India, above the age of 21, and should have a Bachelor’s degree in Science or Engineering from a recognized Indian University or possesses such other equivalent qualifications as the Central Government may specify in this behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must also pass the annual examination conducted by the Controller General of Patents; notifications published on official website and in a prominent newspaper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualifications for registration as a patent agent (Rule 114)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person shall not be eligible to be registered as a patent agent, if he - (a) has been adjudged by a competent court to be of unsound mind; (b) is an undischarged insolvent; (c) being a discharged insolvent, has not obtained from the court a certificate to the effect that his insolvency was caused by misfortune without any misconduct on his part; (d) has been convicted by a competent court ... unless pardoned or disability removed by Central Government; (e) being a legal practitioner has been guilty of professional misconduct; or (f) being a chartered accountant, has been guilty of negligence or misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive fitness and character requirements; Central Government may remove disability in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of patent agents to practice before the Controller (Section 127)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent agent is entitled to practise before the Controller; and to prepare all documents, transact all business and discharge such other functions as may be prescribed in connection with any proceedings before the Controller under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of professional activities of registered patent agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription and verification of documents by authorised patent agent (Section 128)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications and communications to the Controller under this Act may be signed by a patent agent authorised in writing in this behalf by the person concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows parties to appoint agents in writing to sign and verify filings; ensures agent authority is documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on practice as patent agents (Section 129)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a person registered as a patent agent is authorized to practice. In the case of a partnership, the firm may be described or held out as Patent Agent, only if all of the partners of the Firm are registered as patent agents. No company or other body corporate shall practice, describe itself or hold itself out as Patent Agents or permit itself to be so described or held out. Each person in the associate group if any constituted should be a registered Agent and duly authorized by the concerned person on behalf they act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents unregistered firms or corporates from misrepresenting patent-agent services; ensures individuals practicing are registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller may refuse to recognise certain agents (Section 131)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller may refuse to recognise as agent in respect of any business under this Act: (a) any individual whose name has been removed from, and not restored to, the register; (b) any person who has been convicted of an offence under section 123; (c) any person, not being registered as a patent agent, who in the opinion of the Controller is engaged wholly or mainly in acting as agent in applying for patents ...; (d) any company or firm, if any person whom the Controller could refuse to recognise as agent is acting as a director or manager of the company or is a partner in the firm; (e) any person who neither resides nor has a place of business in India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller exercises gatekeeping to prevent unfit or non-resident persons or sham agents from acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to remove name of a patent agent from the Register
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of any person from the Register can be removed if the Controller is satisfied that: (i) his/her name has been entered in the Register by error on account of misrepresentation or suppression of material fact; or (ii) he/she has been convicted of any offence and sentenced to a term of imprisonment or has been guilty of misconduct in his professional capacity which ... renders him unfit to be kept in the register. Also removal can follow request by agent, death, or default in payment of fees for more than three months after due date. The Controller shall take such decision after giving that person a reasonable opportunity of being heard and after any further inquiry, as he thinks fit to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal is published and communicated to the person concerned; procedural fairness (opportunity to be heard) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of names of patent agents (Rule 117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of names of persons removed from the register of Patent Agents can be made by the Controller, on Application made in form 23 within two months from the date of such removal. The restoration of name to the register shall be published and communicated to the person concerned. If the name of a person is entered in the register of Patents Agents, his name shall be continued therein for a period of one year from the date on which his last annual fee became due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is time-limited and formal (Form 23) and is followed by publication; annual fee continuation rule specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contravention of Sections 35 or 39 — offence and punishment (Section 118)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person fails to comply with any direction given under section 35 or makes or causes to be made an application for the grant of a patent in contravention of section 39, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal sanctions apply for certain prohibited communications and directions relating to inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falsification of entries in register (Section 119)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person makes a false entry in any register kept under the Patents Act or provides any writing or evidence as a result of which the entry in the register results into a false entry, then he is punishable with imprisonment for a term that may extend to 2 years or with fine or with both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions protect integrity of official patent registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized claim of patent rights and labeling (Section 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person falsely represents that any article sold by him is patented in India or is the subject of an Application for a Patent in India, he shall be punishable with fine that may extend to rupees one lakh. The use of words 'Patent', 'Patented', 'Patent applied for', 'Patent pending', without mentioning the name of the country means that they are patented in India or Patent applied for in India and attract the provisions of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits deceptive use of patent-related labels and imposes monetary penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrongful use of words 'Patent Office' (Section 121)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person uses on his place of business or any document issued by him which would reasonably lead to the belief that either his place of business is the Patent Office or is officially connected with the Patent Office, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term that may extend to 6 months, or with fine, or with both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects public from misleading claims of official Patent Office status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal or failure to supply information (Sections 100(5) and 146) — penalties (Section 122)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person refuses or fails to furnish information as required under Sections 100(5) and 146 he shall be punishable with fine which may go up to rupees one lakh. Section 100(5) requires information on government use; Section 146 requires annual statement regarding working of the patented invention in India (Form 27). Furnishing false information knowingly attracts imprisonment up to 6 months or fine or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory information duties carry sanctions; working statements must be filed annually within three months of end of year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice by non-registered persons — penalties (Section 123)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person practicing as a Patent Agent without registering himself as such is liable to be punished with a fine of rupees one lakh for the first offence and rupees five lakh for subsequent offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict monetary penalties deter unregistered practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offences by companies and liability of officers (Section 124)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an offence is committed by a company, the company as well as every person such as director, manager, secretary, in charge of, and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business at the time of the commission of the offence, shall be deemed to be guilty and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. The punishment will not be applicable if such person proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or he has taken due care to prevent the offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal liability attaches to responsible officers unless they can show lack of knowledge or due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's powers equivalent to civil court in proceedings (Section 77)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to any rules made in this behalf, the Controller in any proceedings before him under this Act have the powers of a civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ... namely— (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; (b) requiring the discovery and production of any document; (c) receiving evidence on affidavits; (d) issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses or documents; (e) awarding costs; (f) reviewing his own decision on application ...; (g) setting aside an order passed ex parte ...; (h) any other matter which may be prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller enjoys broad adjudicatory powers akin to civil courts for fact-finding, evidence, and procedural remedies; references to CPC and rules provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding costs in Controller proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any order for costs awarded by the Controller in exercise of the powers conferred upon him is executable as a decree of a civil court. In all proceedings before the Controller, costs may be awarded by the Controller, as he considers reasonable, having regard to all the circumstances of the case. However, the amount of costs awarded in respect of any matter set forth in the Fourth Schedule shall not exceed the amount specified therein. The Controller may, in his discretion award a compensatory cost in any proceeding before him which in his opinion is false or vexatious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs are enforceable and subject to Fourth Schedule caps; compensatory costs deter frivolous/vexatious litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by Controller — grounds and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person considering himself aggrieved by any order or decree of the Controller ... who, from the discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him ... or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or for any other sufficient reason, desires to obtain a review ... may apply for a review of the order or decree to the Controller. Application shall be made within one month from the date of communication of such decision or within such further period not exceeding one month as the Controller may allow and shall be accompanied by a statement setting forth the grounds on which the review is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure references: Section 114, Order XLVII CPC, Form-24/Form-4; Controller transmits copies to other concerned persons where decision affects them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for obviating an irregularity (Rule 137)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document for the amendment of which no special provision is made in the Act may be amended and any irregularity in procedure which in the opinion of the Controller may be obviated without detriment to the interests of any person, may be corrected if the Controller thinks fit and upon such terms as he may direct. Only such an irregularity is allowed which is without detriment to the interests of any person. Generally, a failure to act within prescribed time may not be considered as an irregularity which can be obviated under this Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited curative amendments and correction of procedural irregularities but not to the prejudice of parties; time-defaults usually excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentioning inventor in patent — grounds, timing and procedure (Section 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Controller is satisfied, upon a request or claim made in accordance with the provisions of this section— (i) that the person in respect of or by whom the request or claim is made is the inventor of an invention in respect of which application for a patent has been made, or of a substantial part of that invention; and (ii) that the application for the patent is a direct consequence of his being the inventor, the Controller shall ... cause him to be mentioned as inventor in any patent granted ... Such a request or claim shall be accompanied by a statement setting out the circumstances. A request or claim shall be made before the grant of patent. The Controller shall give notice of the claim to every applicant for the patent (not being the claimant) and to any other person whom the Controller may consider to be interested and before deciding upon any such request or claim, the Controller shall, if required, hear the person in respect of or by whom the request or claim is made, and also any person to whom notice of the claim has been given. Where any person has been mentioned as inventor ... any other person who alleges that he ought not to have been so mentioned may at any time apply to the Controller for a certificate to that effect, and the Controller may, after hearing, if required, issue such a certificate and rectify the specification and the register accordingly. The procedure specified in rules 55A and 57 to 63 relating to filing of notice of opposition, written statement, reply statement, leaving evidence, hearing and cost shall, so far as may be, apply to the hearing of such a claim or application as they apply to the opposition proceedings subject to modification that reference to patentee shall be construed as the person making the claim or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a full adversarial procedure for inventor-mention claims analogous to opposition proceedings; ensures right to be heard and rectification mechanisms.
